concepts.title: Nervous System - Neurons and Reflex Action

questions.q: What is a neuron and what does it do?
questions.a: A nerve cell specialised to carry electrical impulses from receptors to the brain/spinal cord and onward to muscles or glands.

questions.q: Why can you withdraw your hand from a hot object without thinking?
questions.a: A reflex arc through the spinal cord acts at once - the brain only learns of it afterwards.

questions.q: Which parts of the brain control involuntary actions?
questions.a: Medulla in the hindbrain controls breathing, heartbeat etc.; cerebellum keeps balance and posture.

questions.q: How does the touch-me-not plant fold its leaves so quickly?
questions.a: Water shifts out of cells at the leaf bases changing their shape - a fast, non-growth movement.

questions.q: Which hormone bends a shoot towards light?
questions.a: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, elongating it so the shoot bends toward light.

questions.q: Name one growth-dependent and one growth-independent plant movement.
questions.a: Growth: tendril coiling, phototropism. Non-growth: folding of mimosa leaves.

questions.q: What is the role of adrenaline in the body?
questions.a: It readies the body for emergency: faster heartbeat, breathing and blood supply to muscles.

questions.q: Why is insulin essential in the blood?
questions.a: It regulates blood sugar; too little insulin causes diabetes with high sugar levels.

questions.q: How do hormones differ from nerve messages?
questions.a: Hormones travel in blood, act slowly but longer; nerve impulses are electrical, fast and short-lived.
